instruction: `ds/counter.py::Counter.increment` loses updates under concurrent use. It performs a read-modify-write without holding the lock: it reads the current value, yields, then writes the incremented value back, so when multiple threads call `increment()` at the same time the final value ends up lower than the total number of increments.
gold_patch:
diff --git a/ds/counter.py b/ds/counter.py
--- a/ds/counter.py
+++ b/ds/counter.py
@@ -13,10 +13,8 @@
 
     def increment(self, n=1):
         """Add ``n`` to the counter and return the new value."""
-        current = self._value
-        current += n
-        time.sleep(0)
-        self._value = current
+        with self._lock:
+            self._value += n
         return self._value
 
     @property
